## Worktree-Isolation Investigation Detail (for later analysis)

Detected during internal dogfooding of /dso:sprint waxen-sigma. Two of eight isolation:worktree dispatches across two batches ran UN-isolated and wrote into the session worktree instead of an isolated agent worktree.

### Occurrences (2 of 8 dispatches)
| Batch | Task | Agent type | Outcome | agentId / transcript |
|-------|------|-----------|---------|----------------------|
| L0 | b5fd-7682 | dso:red-test-writer | LEAKED | a3dd4ca9bba3376f5 |
| L0 | 5e96-ea32 | general-purpose | isolated OK | ac6b4f4e43f34ed5e |
| L0 | 55c7-f127 | dso:red-test-writer | isolated OK | a019f7c13d2d3e811 |
| L0 | 315a-77fb | general-purpose | isolated OK | a23215ee70e2bd8b6 |
| L1 | 3da3-a959 | general-purpose | LEAKED | a616dc9a6b2a2903d |
| L1 | 2298-45c0 | general-purpose | isolated OK | a7772b85366a07abe |
| L1 | 71bb-83b5 | general-purpose | isolated OK | aca7a4de7ed0a016f |

Transcript output files live under the session tasks dir:
/private/tmp/claude-502/-Users-joeoakhart-digital-service-orchestra-worktrees-worktree-20260602-122923/<run>/tasks/<agentId>.output

### Reliable diagnostic signal
The task-completion notification's <worktree> block presence/absence perfectly separated isolated from leaked dispatches:
- isolated (6): notification carried <worktree><worktreePath>.../agent-<id></worktreePath>...; an agent-<id> entry appeared in `git worktree list`.
- leaked (2): notification had NO <worktree> block; NO agent-<id> worktree was ever created; the sub-agent's own `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` resolved to the SESSION worktree; the agent's new file appeared staged in the session worktree (`git status --short`).

### What it is NOT
- NOT the prompt-path-leak failure mode (6b67-2aad / 1053-4ec3): dispatch prompts contained only SESSION_BRANCH (a branch name), SESSION_HEAD (a sha), and relative paths — no session-worktree absolute path. The agents correctly derived paths from their own `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`; that simply resolved to the session worktree because no isolated worktree was allocated for that dispatch.
- NOT agent-type-specific: leaks hit both dso:red-test-writer (b5fd) and general-purpose (3da3).
- NOT reaping (907d): the worktree was never created in the first place (no agent-<id> ever in `git worktree list`), as opposed to created-then-removed.

### Conditions / hypotheses to test later
- Both leaks involved a single-new-file write; both occurred in batches dispatched as 3–4 parallel isolation:worktree Agent calls in one message. Hypothesis: a race / nondeterministic allocation failure in the harness worktree provisioning under parallel dispatch (since siblings in the same batch isolated fine, it is per-dispatch flaky, not batch-wide).
- Reproduction signal to capture next time: log whether the notification carries a <worktree> block; cross-check `git worktree list` immediately after dispatch.
- Harness: Claude Code desktop, isolation:"worktree". Capture exact harness version on recurrence.

### Recovery used (worked both times, no data loss)
Back up staged session changes to a patch -> `git stash` to clean the session tree -> `git worktree add agent-<task>-recovered -b worktree-agent-<task>-recovered <session-HEAD>` -> restore files + .test-index entry from the patch -> record-test-status -> commit (with DSO-Story trailer, WITHOUT copying .sprint-active) -> harvest-worktree.sh -> drop stash. This mirrors per-worktree-review-commit.md Step 1a Tier-2 RECOVERED_FROM_SESSION.
